_about: Which Envil/IPC DEFAULT rules get pushed INTO the KiCad project so they show in KiCad's Design Rule Editor. Flat numeric floors merge (as max) into board.design_settings.rules (the Constraints page); conditional IPC rules (voltage clearance) are generated from ipc_constraints.json and written as custom rules into <project>.kicad_dru, in the SAME managed file the user rules use. Defaults sit UNDER the user overlay (precedence USER > DEFAULT). Pure data — no numbers duplicated here; the voltage table is read live from ipc_constraints.json.
_layering: set_design_rules order: (1) fab profile -> Constraints, (2) THESE class floors max()'d on top, (3) user/project overrides on top (can go looser with a warning). DRU file = default voltage-clearance rules + user directives, regenerated together.
_apply_on_create_project_comment: When true, create_project runs set_design_rules on the brand-new empty project so the default rules (fab Constraints + net classes + IPC voltage-clearance .kicad_dru) are written immediately — they show in KiCad's Design Rule Editor the first time the project is opened, before any build. Set false to only write defaults when a build / 'apply design rules' runs.

acceptance_class_floors._comment: Apply the acceptance-class minimums from ipc_constraints.json:acceptance_classes[default_acceptance_class] as a floor (max) on the matching KiCad Constraints key. Only annular ring maps to a KiCad DRC check (plating thickness is a fab spec KiCad does not verify). map: ipc_constraints class field -> kicad rules key.

voltage_clearance_rules._comment: Generate IPC-2221B clearance-by-voltage custom rules (KiCad's flat Constraints page cannot express 'clearance depends on net voltage'). One rule per distinct clearance tier, keyed on a high-voltage NET CLASS the user assigns their net to. Read live from ipc_constraints.json:clearance_by_voltage.bands using the column named in `condition_field`. Bands at/below `min_voltage_v` are skipped (already covered by the fab/default clearance). netclass name = `{netclass_prefix}{bandMaxV}V` (e.g. HV_300V). These rules are visible in the Design Rule Editor immediately and become active the moment a net is put in that class.

width_by_current_rules._comment: Generate IPC-2152 minimum-track-WIDTH-by-current custom rules (KiCad's flat Constraints page has only ONE global min-track-width; it cannot say 'a 3 A rail must be >= 1.7 mm'). One rule per current band, keyed on a current NET CLASS the user assigns their power net to. Read live from ipc_constraints.json:width_by_current.bands (1 oz external copper, ~10-20 degC rise — heavier copper carries more at the same width). netclass name = `{netclass_prefix}{bandMaxA}A` (e.g. I_3A). Bands at/below `min_current_a` are skipped (already covered by the fab/default min width). Visible in the Design Rule Editor immediately; active the moment a net is put in that class.

auto_assign_electrical._comment: Auto-assign nets to the HV_*/I_* net classes above so the IPC-2221B clearance + IPC-2152 width rules ACTIVATE without the user hand-assigning each net. Runs in set_design_rules after the pin-role classifier: parses a voltage/current magnitude embedded in the NET NAME (e.g. '+48V', '400VDC', '3V3', 'MOTOR_5A') and maps it to the covering tier via default_rules.netclass_for_voltage/current. VOLTAGE is on by default — a name-embedded voltage is a strong, low-false-positive signal and a too-tight HV clearance only widens spacing. CURRENT is OFF by default: a wrong I_* assignment forces a wide trace that can break routing, and net names rarely encode current reliably; enable it only for boards whose power nets are named with their current.

pcb_rule_severities._comment: PCB DRC rule-severity overrides written into board.design_settings.rule_severities of the .kicad_pro so KiCad's STORED DRC profile reflects fab/manufacturability intent instead of stock defaults (mirrors what _erc_rule_severities does for the schematic). Our drc_check runs --severity-all so it always REPORTS every check regardless; this affects KiCad's GUI DRC and the ship_design export gate (which counts stored 'error's). Conservative: promote manufacturability checks KiCad ships as 'ignore' up to 'warning', keep prototype-stage noise as 'warning', leave the hard fab-critical checks as 'error'. Values must be one of error|warning|ignore. The user can flip any rule in Board Setup -> Design Rules -> Violation Severity.
